description:
A file whose top-level code calls a module defined above it never builds main/0 and fails with "resolve/unknown-function: function `main/0` is not defined --> <generated>". This is the distiller's next stop: its last line is `Distill.main(System.argv())`.

    defmodule M do
      def go(a), do: dbg(a)
    end
    M.go(1)

Elixir 1.19.4 runs it. Elixir refuses `require M` and `import M` of a module defined in the same context ("module M is not loaded but was defined ..."). fz today gives the main/0 error for require and "waited on an executable's runtime demand with no ready producer" for import. `alias M` and a require inside a separate defmodule already work in both.

Cause (read from code and telemetry, confirmed by the first red test): the top-level ScopeCode job waits on ModuleDefined(M) to learn whether M.go is a macro. When woken it re-walks the file, and discover_modules -> index_body (identity.rs:431) stores ModuleState::Indexed unconditionally (update_if_changed, identity.rs:885). This demotes M from Defined, so module_defined_revision (world.rs:1738) is None again and the job waits forever. At drain, unresolved_issue (world.rs:2558) drops ModuleDefined/ModuleInterface waits through a catch-all `_ => None`, leaving only the root's main/0 wait to report.

Design: page /Users/j5n/Workspace/fz-sc8.41.html, APPROVED 2026-10-30. Three decisions, each made once:
1. ModuleState reconcile keeps a Scoped/Defined module when re-indexed from the same source (no revision change); a different source still resets it.
2. apply_require/apply_import refuse a module defined by the requiring scope, with Elixir's message at the require/import span.
3. unresolved_issue matches FactKey exhaustively; ModuleDefined/ModuleInterface go to unresolved_module_issue; kinds that are never a user cause become an explicit internal-error issue.

Done when: identity unit test (same source keeps Defined, different source resets); oracle fixture for a top-level call to a module defined above (interp/run/build match elixir); diagnostic fixtures for same-context require, require of a macro, import, and nested defmodule require; a drive test that a stalled ModuleDefined of a never-defined module reports "module `X` is not defined" with its span; telemetry shows the predicted succession (ScopeCode twice, DefineModule once, no ModuleIndexed change on the second walk); full unmasked pin census, no rise; docs updated; the distiller re-run and its next error reported.
title: Once a module is defined it stays defined; same-context require/import is refused as in Elixir
